skill.name: service-mesh-expert
skill.description: Expert service mesh architect for Istio, Linkerd, and cloud-native networking patterns.
skill.summary: Designs service mesh architecture, traffic policy, zero-trust security, observability, and multi-cluster operations.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 20 uses Markdown inline backticks around a referenced resource path and does not execute Ruby, shell, or any external command.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 20 only formats resources/implementation-playbook.md as inline Markdown code. There is no Ruby backtick expression, shell command, or executable code path.

content.value_statement: Service mesh adoption can create unclear traffic, security, and observability decisions. This skill gives structured guidance for Istio, Linkerd, Kubernetes networking, and zero-trust mesh operations.
actual_capabilities: Designs Istio and Linkerd installation and configuration plans.
Defines routing, load balancing, circuit breaker, retry, and traffic split patterns.
Recommends mTLS, certificate, authorization policy, and zero-trust networking practices.
Plans distributed tracing, metrics, logs, and mesh overhead monitoring.
Guides multi-cluster or multi-cloud mesh federation and service discovery.
Creates operational runbooks for failover, resilience testing, and policy rollout.
limitations: Does not execute cluster commands or inspect live Kubernetes resources by itself.
Requires current topology, platform, and security requirements from the user.
Guidance depends on mesh versions, cloud provider constraints, and installed observability tools.
Does not replace production change review, load testing, or security approval.

use_cases.title: Plan an Istio Rollout
use_cases.description: Create an adoption plan with prerequisites, namespace rollout order, policy stages, and validation checks.

use_cases.title: Harden Service Communication
use_cases.description: Map service-to-service requirements into mTLS modes, authorization policies, certificate handling, and audit steps.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot Mesh Reliability
use_cases.description: Analyze routing, retries, circuit breakers, load balancing, and observability signals for failed requests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Mesh
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new Kubernetes service mesh.
prompt_templates.prompt: I run Kubernetes services in [environment]. Create an Istio or Linkerd adoption plan with prerequisites, risks, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Canary Traffic
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate release planning with traffic management controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design traffic management for a canary release of [service]. Include routing, retries, circuit breakers, metrics, and rollback checks.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Mesh Security
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security design for zero-trust service communication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my service communication requirements: [details]. Recommend mTLS mode, authorization policy structure, certificate handling, and rollout sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Cluster Federation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for multi-cluster or multi-cloud mesh operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-cluster mesh architecture for [clusters and clouds]. Cover service discovery, failover, observability, security boundaries, and runbooks.

output_examples.input: A platform team wants to introduce Istio without breaking existing Kubernetes services.
output_examples.output: A staged rollout plan with namespace selection, permissive mTLS, telemetry checks, sidecar sizing guidance, and clear promotion gates.

output_examples.input: A security team needs stronger service-to-service controls for payment workloads.
output_examples.output: A zero-trust policy outline covering strict mTLS, authorization boundaries, certificate rotation, exception handling, and audit evidence.

output_examples.input: An SRE team sees intermittent errors after adding retries to a mesh route.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path that checks retry budgets, timeout settings, circuit breakers, destination rules, and trace data.

best_practices: Start in permissive mTLS mode, verify telemetry, then enforce strict mode by namespace.
Define routing and resilience policies before high-risk releases.
Monitor latency, resource use, and trace coverage after each mesh change.
anti_patterns: Enforcing strict mTLS across all namespaces before identifying unsupported workloads.
Treating service mesh as a substitute for application-level authorization.
Adding retries without timeouts, circuit breakers, or clear error budgets.

faq.question: Which service mesh platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on Istio and Linkerd, with general cloud-native networking guidance for Kubernetes environments.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready mesh policies?
faq.answer: It can draft policy designs and validation steps. Production changes still need review, testing, and environment-specific checks.

faq.question: Does it support zero-trust networking work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers mTLS, authorization policy design, certificate handling, and gradual enforcement strategies.

faq.question: Can it help with canary or blue-green deployments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan routing, traffic splitting, metrics, rollback checks, and resilience policies.

faq.question: Does it inspect my live Kubernetes cluster?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance from the information you share and does not run cluster commands.

faq.question: What input should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Share mesh platform, Kubernetes version, service topology, security goals, current policies, and observability tools.
